To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

earnings reported under IASB IFRS in an emerging market are timelier than earnings reported under national accounting standards, and that earnings reported under the national accounting standards of an emerging market become less timely over time as a result of the adoption of IASB IAS and convergence with IASB IFSRS.

earnings reported under the Chinese accounting standards have a lower earnings-response-coefficient, but a higher response coefficient for future earnings, than earnings reported according to International Financial Reporting Standards before the Chinese accounting standards converged with the International Financial Reporting Standards in 2007, but that the response coefficient for future Chinese earnings has continued to increase since the convergence.
the timeliness in recognition of earnings reported by Chinese firms under Chinese GAAP has deteriorated over time as a result of the series of harmonization with IFRS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of harmonization with IFRS and convergence with IAS/IFRS on the timeliness and quality of earnings reported under national GAAP.
the effects of harmonization or convergence on the timeliness and quality of earnings reported under the national accounting standards in emerging capital markets.
the effects of harmonization with IFRS, and convergence with IASB standards, on the timeliness and reliability of earnings reported under national accounting standards in emerging Chinese markets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of harmonization with IFRS may be positive, but may also be neutral or even negative, depending on the country-specific institutional environment.
the effects of harmonizing and convergencing national accounting standards with the IFRS on accounting quality in emerging capital markets are ambiguous.
the convergence of Chinese GAAP with IFRS has had a negative impact on the quality of earnings reported under IAS/IFRS in China.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
harmonization and convergence of Chinese GAAP with IFRS have not improved the quality of earnings reported under the Chinese GAAP.

the timeliness and quality of earnings reported under national accounting standards in emerging markets can be affected by the extent of harmonization and/or convergence with IFRSthe more harmonized or converged, the less timely the reported earnings.
, the convergence with IFRs in China does not improve the quality of financial reporting.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the effects of harmonizing and convering national accounting standards with international standards in emerging markets may depend on the level of development of accounting standards in those countries.
the quality of earnings information reported under Chinese GAAS has been declining over time, and this is likely due to the increasing use of the IFRS-based accounting standards in China.
harmonizing and/or converging national accounting systems with IFRS may not be sufficient for emerging markets to increase accounting quality.
